title: Let protection become felt, not recited
summary: The shabad names the Lord as Father, Mother, relative, and brother until protection becomes intimate. Let shelter become personal enough to be trusted.
takeaway: Name the Protector as near kin, not a distant idea.
lifeApplication: When fear makes you feel exiled, speak one relationship-name from the line and let it bring shelter back into the body.

source.shortMeaning: The Lord is named as Father, Mother, relative, and brother, turning protection into closeness.
source.lifeApplication: When fear rises, make protection personal enough to steady you.

evidence.coreClaim: Fear softens when divine protection is not abstract but named as the nearest family.
evidence.turn: Fear thins when shelter becomes personal again.
evidence.practicalImplication: When fear makes you feel exiled, speak one relationship-name from the line and let it bring shelter back into the body.
